title: Meridian Motion — make or buy
decision_question: Should Meridian Motion manufacture precision housings in-house in 2027, lease a flexible cell, or continue buying from an external supplier?

initial_hypothesis.statement: Buy an owned machining cell in 2027 because $46 of internal variable cost is below the supplier quote.
initial_hypothesis.explanation: The proposed owned cell breaches the 2027 capex cap and cash floor, while including scrap and fixed costs removes most apparent variable-cost savings; a reversible supply/lease path is viable.

key_insights.text: Owned cell requires $7.30M upfront, above $5.00M capex cap and leaves only $1.90M cash versus $4.00M floor.
2028 supplier cost $7.50M, owned cell operating cost $5.54M before recovery of capex; three-year owned total $24.09M versus supplier $22.50M.
The $46 vs $73 comparison mixes cost per started unit and factory-gate price; correct supplier cost is $75 per accepted delivered unit.
The 98.5% internal yield excludes start-up, rework and downtime; use 8% first-year and 4% subsequent scrap scenarios.
Leased-cell three-year total including setup is $22.20M on plan volumes, but its forecast has capacity, contract and downtime risk.
Supplier reliability is 96.8% against a 97% requirement; reserve capacity and build contingency rather than treat make-or-buy as only a cost choice.

required_calculations.text: Own cell 2027 cash after up-front spending

decision_relevant_evidence.text: Five-million capex cap and four-million liquidity floor
Scrap, fixed costs and start-up time
Accepted-unit vs started-unit and freight definitions

contradictory_evidence: Cheap internal variable cost vs full ownership cost
Owned plants have fewer delays but different scale and demand patterns

reasoning_traps.text: Taking 98.5% demo yield as the first-year production rate
Comparing $46 per started unit with $73 factory-gate buying cost
Ignoring the capex cap or minimum liquidity
Treating cross-plant delay correlation as proof of insourcing causality

key_tradeoffs.text: Supplier concentration vs new operating capability

plausible_recommendations.text: Keep outsourcing with reserved second-source capacity and time-boxed lease feasibility, with volume and service gates.
Install a flexible leased cell if independently validated reliability, site readiness and throughput justify the setup and annual fixed charge.
Approve the $7.3M owned cell now under the present board constraints.

defensibility_criteria: Compare accepted-unit fully loaded economics and cash constraints
Address contract service reliability and contingent capacity
Distinguish factory-gate and delivered costs, demo and real yields
State evidence needed before any irrevocable build

decision_requirements.question: Does each option satisfy capital and minimum cash?
Were yields, costs and units normalized?
Are build/lease decisions gated on true demand?
decision_requirements.unnecessary_if: if only outsourcing is recommended with an explicit reassessment
